title: From the Editor — A Shadow on the Glass
settingText: A road town in brutal daylight above, with a cool dark stair descending below street level into the Mirage Club. Use the contrast between white exterior glare and deep interior shadow. No character reveal and no readable signage.
summary: Art-directed opening editorial splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 3. Entice the reader, establish the live pressure and world feeling, and preserve the story page-one reveal.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Names are expensive in the Sunfields.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Some can get you a bed. Some can get you shot. Some come with debts that survived the people who earned them.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: So there are places where nobody asks.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Beneath one of the road towns, the Mirage Club has made an entire refuge out of that bargain: leave the world upstairs, leave your history with it, and let everybody be whoever they say they are.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: After the Last Drop and Cinder Basin, Brandon could use a place like that.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For once, nobody should care what his name is.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Should.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Welcome to the Mirage.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: — Jeff Hines

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Star Splitter Visions

title: No Names Below
summary: The Mirage Club is a refuge built around a strict social rule: nobody asks for a real name below street level. Isabella breaks that rule the moment she sees Brandon and calls him Merritt.

panelPlan.text: Wide interior: subterranean club during a quiet performance interval, crowded but intimate. A hand-painted sign by the stairs reads NO NAMES BELOW.
Brandon, Eva and Jessie enter looking for shade and a meal. Isabella stops mid-conversation across the room when she sees Brandon.
She crosses the floor and says Merritt. The room goes noticeably quiet; several patrons glance toward the painted NO NAMES BELOW notice at the stairs.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: You came back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm not Merritt.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Don't stand there like you don't know me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: He doesn't know anybody here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I do know the rule says no names.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: The rule can survive one name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Can I eat first?

title: The Room Takes Sides
summary: Isabella accuses Brandon of abandoning the club during an old crackdown. Because she has broken the no-names rule, the club splits over whether her grievance deserves an exception. Brandon becomes the center of a conflict he does not own.

panelPlan.text: Isabella denies Brandon his attempt to retreat into supper; she and Brandon face each other at a copper table. Patrons deliberately turn chairs away while still listening.
A longtime patron tells Isabella to drop it; another says Merritt owes the room an answer. Eva watches the social fault line spread.
Brandon sets his untouched drink aside and asks Isabella one concrete question: what does she actually want from the man she thinks he is?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Not yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I was afraid of that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: You left us with chains on the doors.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: What did you need to say to Merritt?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: That he left us here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then say it. I'll listen.

title: The Man Who Promised
summary: Eva learns that Isabella was not merely surprised by Brandon: a traveling preacher recently told her that Merritt would return before the next flare. Jessie recognizes that this is no longer just rumor chasing them.

panelPlan.text: After Isabella finally says what she needed Merritt to hear, she tells Eva to ask the next question. In a side corridor, Eva follows Isabella while Jessie waits by the stairs. Isabella retrieves an old photograph with a man's face partly burned away; the resemblance to Brandon is suggestive but not conclusive.
Isabella says the preacher knew details about Merritt he should not have known. Eva's excitement finally gives way to unease.
Jessie takes the photograph, compares it to Brandon across the room, and hands it back without declaring a match.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Who told you he was coming?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: A preacher. Samuel, if that was his name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: What did he ask for?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Nothing. Sat at the bar and let me do most of the talking.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Then he said Merritt might come back before the flare.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Did you tell him what Merritt looked like?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: I showed him the photograph after he said the name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: So he already knew.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: He knew enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That's the first real lead we've had.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: It's also proof somebody got here first.

title: What He Left
summary: Isabella brings Brandon to the locked room Merritt abandoned years earlier. Instead of arguing about resemblance, Brandon helps her face what was actually left behind: ordinary possessions and no grand explanation.

panelPlan.text: Isabella takes them to what Merritt left behind and unlocks a cramped storage room. Dust lies thick on objects nobody has moved in years. Brandon stays at the threshold until she enters first.
They find a coat, a broken instrument case, letters never sent. Eva hangs back, understanding that curiosity has limits.
Isabella holds one letter but cannot open it. Brandon takes no object and makes no claim on Merritt's life.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Then stop theorizing and look at what he left.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: People say they'll come back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: You really don't want to know what's in the letter?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Not if it was written for him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: We can go.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Stay.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Why?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: You've been in everybody else's business all afternoon. You can stay for the hard part.

title: One Lie Too Many
summary: Eva proposes a test: tell the club Brandon is someone entirely different and see whether the story changes. Brandon refuses to turn Isabella's grief into an experiment, establishing a boundary that will matter when Raina's methods are revealed.

panelPlan.text: Eva insists she can stand still and still have an idea; near the stairs she quietly proposes giving the room a false name to see who repeats it.
Brandon stops walking. His objection is not about being studied; it is about using Isabella and the room as instruments.
Isabella overhears enough to understand. Instead of being offended by Brandon, she directs her anger at the unseen preacher who primed her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I can stand still and still have an idea.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: What if we give them a name Samuel couldn't know? Something ridiculous.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Don't use Isabella as a test.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: It could tell us whether somebody is carrying the story.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Samuel already used me once. Don't do it again.

title: A Shadow on the Glass
summary: The trio leaves with a concrete lead, Samuel, but no explanation for why the planted story fit Isabella's history so well. In the club's street-level glass, Brandon's reflection briefly overlays the damaged photograph, an ordinary visual coincidence that lands harder because everyone is looking for meaning.

panelPlan.text: At the stairs, Isabella returns the old photograph to its envelope rather than giving it to Eva. She and Brandon exchange a restrained goodbye; neither treats him as Merritt.
Outside, Eva writes Samuel in her small ledger. Jessie asks where she intends to look for a preacher in the whole Sunfields.
Final panel: in dusty storefront glass, Brandon's reflection lines up with the burned-away half of the photograph still visible through Isabella's hand inside. It could be nothing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Find him instead.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: If we do, what do you want said?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Tell Samuel I remember his face.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: We have Samuel, maybe. And a coat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Can we go now?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Do you think Brandon actually wants to know?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: He listens every time you start.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Then he gets back on the road.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That doesn't mean he doesn't care.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They finally have a name for the man arriving first.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Samuel.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A preacher with a talent for putting the right story in the right ear.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: But a name is not an explanation.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: At the next relay, someone is already waiting for Brandon.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Not eventually.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Today.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
